preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**6 for x in [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]]) and all(1 <= int(y) <= 10**6 for y in [int(line.split()[1]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]])
preconditions.description: All glade numbers in trails are integers between 1 and 1,000,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()) == m + 1 and all(len(line.split()) == 2 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Input has exactly m+1 lines: first line contains n and m, followed by m lines of trail pairs.
First line contains integers n (number of glades) and m (number of trails) matching the problem statement.

postconditions.expression: stdout == '0' if (all(degree % 2 == 0 for degree in degrees.values()) and degrees[1] > 0) else min_additional_edges
postconditions.description: Output is 0 if and only if the graph is Eulerian (all vertices have even degree and glade 1 has at least one trail). Otherwise, output is the minimum number of edges to add to make the graph Eulerian.

postconditions.expression: (min_additional_edges := (sum(1 for degree in degrees.values() if degree % 2 != 0) // 2)) if not (all(degree % 2 == 0 for degree in degrees.values()) and degrees[1] > 0) else 0
postconditions.description: If the graph is not Eulerian, the minimum number of edges to add is half the number of vertices with odd degree (rounded up).

invariants.expression: (degrees := {i: 0 for i in range(1, n + 1)}) and all(degrees.update({x: degrees.get(x, 0) + 1, y: degrees.get(y, 0) + 1}) for x, y in [(int(line.split()[0]), int(line.split()[1])) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]])
invariants.description: degrees is a dictionary where degrees[i] is the number of trails connected to glade i, computed from the input trails.
